newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-S.AFRICA SEEK REPORT ON TEST LOSS TO INDIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-S.AFRICA SEEK REPORT ON TEST LOSS TO INDIA.

text.p: South Africa's cricket board has asked the International Cricket Council (ICC) for the referee's match report on the first test against India, South African manager Robbie Muzelle said on Thursday.
"A request was made by the team management to ICC referee John Reid for a copy of the report he submitted on the Ahmedabad test," Muzelle told reporters.
The request followed an angry comment from coach Bob Woolmer that the team had been "stuffed" before the test because wickets and practice facilities were not what the South Africans had wanted.
Woolmer said on Sunday that he was unhappy with the pitch and the practice facilities for his team.
The match ended in Ahmedabad on Saturday in a 64-run win for India after South Africa were bundled out for 105 runs in their second innings on a wearing wicket.
Muzelle said Ali Bacher, managing director of the United Cricket Board of South Africa, had asked for a copy of the report.
Muzelle quoted Reid as saying the board should ask the ICC for the report, and that he was not obliged to provide the report, or even the gist of it, to the concerned teams.
"I think it is but fair that the teams should also know about the report," Muzelle said. "Anyway, that match is gone and we have started a new part of the tour. We do not want to take up the issue."
South Africa are currently playing their second test against India in the eastern city of Calcutta.
